matt_devops: Hey team — customer `acme-inc` on Private VPC can't reach our inference endpoint (dedicated pool). They see TLS handshake timeouts from their app. Packet logs show SYNs leaving their NAT but no ACK from the endpoint. :frowning:

sophie_support: Thanks — which endpoint + customer subnet? Any repro steps we can run from a bastion?

matt_devops: endpoint: private-infer-1.redwood.internal:443, customer subnet CIDR 10.50.8.0/24. Repro steps they ran from their app: curl -v https://private-infer-1.redwood.internal -> hangs on "TLS handshake" and eventually times out. They sent a small tcpdump from their NAT: ```
14:02:11.345678 IP 34.120.45.10.52000 > 10.200.30.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
14:02:11.346001 IP 34.120.45.10.52001 > 10.200.30.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0
# repeated SYNs, no SYN/ACKs visible
```

samir_infra: Two quick checks: 1) security groups are stateful so if SG allows outbound 443 we should be fine, 2) NACLs are stateless — you must allow both inbound and outbound ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for return traffic. Common failure: NACL has a deny for ephemeral range. Also confirm NAT gateway SNAT: the source port on their side will be ephemeral.

matt_devops: I verified SG outbound rule exists for 0.0.0.0/0:443. I ran: ```aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filter "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abc123" --query 'NetworkAcls[].Entries'``` and saw an entry: `DENY 1024-65535 tcp` (priority 100). Oof.

infra-bot: Automated check: NAT egress IP 34.120.45.10 seen reaching endpoint at 2026-01-12T14:02:11Z. No SYN/ACK from endpoint to that IP on return ports. Possible NACL drop on return. :robot_face:

sophie_support: If NACL is denying ephemeral outbound/inbound we should either add explicit allow for ephemeral range or re-order/remove the deny. Customer can't change their managed NACL easily — recommend we add a short-lived allow on their subnet's NACL (both directions) or ask them to relax the deny. Planning/beta: schedule 10m window?

samir_infra: Suggested minimal fix (AWS NACL): ```
# allow ephemeral return traffic (both directions)
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 110 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress false --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 111 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress true  --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```
Note: NACL rules are order-dependent; ensure the allow is evaluated before a broader deny. Also double-check the rule numbers don't collide.

matt_devops: Applied a temporary allow for 10 minutes (rule 110/111) and asked the customer to retry. They report TLS handshake now completes and inference requests succeed.

ops_oncall: Confirmed monitoring spikes show successful 200 responses from private-infer-1 starting at 14:05Z. Rolling the temporary ACL change to permanent after change window — leaving in place until after postmortem. :white_check_mark:

sophie_support: Great — follow-up items: 1) document this as KB: NACL ephemeral port gotcha for private inference, 2) notify account team to suggest persistent NACL change or move to dedicated SG-managed NAT, 3) add a watch to detect NACL denies on ephemeral range for Private customers.

matt_devops: Will write the KB and ping sales. Thanks everyone! :tada:
